summary.headline: RBZ Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 60% YoY to INR121 crores, with EBITDA up 39% to INR18 crores at a 14.9% margin.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR121 crores, up 60% YoY, in line with prior guidance, led by retail at INR78 crores (+70% YoY). EBITDA rose 39% to INR18 crores (14.9% margin) and PAT rose 28% to INR9 crores (7.5% margin). Management attributed margin pressure to muted gold price inventory gains, lease amortisation of INR76 lakhs, lease liabilities of INR115 lakhs, and pre-opening costs for the Surat store. The call focused on the store rollout (four stores this fiscal), a shift toward a gold metal loan (GML) based hedging model, and a long-term target of 75:25 retail to B2B mix.

segments.name: Retail (Harit Zaveri Jewellers)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR78 crores, up 70% YoY. Ahmedabad store grew from INR24 crores turnover in FY21 to INR408 crores in FY26. Share of retail in B2B/B2C mix targeted at 50:50 in one to two years and 75:25 long term.

segments.name: Wholesale (B2B)
segments.commentary: Revenue reported as 42 (unit not clear, likely INR crores), up 47% YoY. Management says order book is strong for the coming quarter and B2B volumes grew.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Revenue approximately INR1.2 crores. Job work is 54% of mix per management, and management is seeking customer gold advances to reduce working capital.

guidance_outlook: Surat store (large format, ~10,000 sq ft) to open around late September 2026, ahead of Navratri (11 October); capex about INR10 crores; 52-60 staff hired.
Rajkot large-format store to open before October/early Q3; Maninagar and Gandhinagar mid-format stores in Q3 (possibly November).
Management expects Q2 performance in line with earlier projections, supported by IIJS order book; July and August order books described as full.
Capex break-even targeted within about one year per store; large-format inventory deployment INR125-150 crores, small-format around INR50 crores.
Debt-to-equity expected below 1:1 (about 0.8 debt to 1 equity) by fiscal year end; medium-term target 1.5-2:1 via GML.
Sanctioned debt of about INR300 crores, not yet fully utilised.
Inventory valued at about INR400 crores; market value about 18% above book.
Employee costs expected to keep rising as store and senior hiring continues; marketing spend to rise.
capex_capacity: Total factory capacity 1.8-2 tonnes a year; current consumption about 900-1,000 kg, around 50% utilisation.
Seasonal utilisation reaches 70-85%, sometimes near 90%, in peak months (July-September).
Surat store capex about INR10 crores; large-format inventory INR125-150 crores; small-format about INR50 crores (plus or minus 10-15%).
Plan to roll out about seven stores in total; four are in this fiscal year, and a few more have leases signed, some in Gujarat.
Retail inventory around 350 kg per an analyst question, not confirmed by management.
demand_pricing: IIJS show described as strong, with good buyer growth and order book; corporate design appreciation noted.
18-karat share of corporate sales: 0% before December, targeted at least 20% by year end.
Management says gold in USD fell about 30% from peak; INR gold has been flat, leaving negligible inventory gain in Q1.
Management says it does not expect 18-karat occasion wear demand to rise across India; 22-karat remains dominant.
Retail Q1 volume about 49 kg versus B2B about 125 kg; own production about 15-20% of retail volume.

qa_highlights.question: Expected timeline, investment and break-even for new stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Surat in Q2, Rajkot early Q3, Maninagar and Gandhinagar in Q3. Large-format capex break-even within a year or less.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term retail vs wholesale mix and debt-equity target?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B:B2C targeted at 50:50 in one to two years and 75:25 long term. Debt-equity below 1:1 by year end, rising to 1.5-2:1 via GML at about 3-3.5% cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline year on year?
qa_highlights.answer: Negligible inventory gain as gold rate was flat, INR76 lakh lease amortisation, INR115 lakh lease liabilities, and pre-opening staff and marketing costs for Surat. Management estimated the total impact at about INR9 crores.

qa_highlights.question: How will the GML hedging work and what share of inventory will be hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: Gradual move toward hedging, with about 50% in year two and 75% in year three. Retail cash flows will repay GML sub-limits. Bank negotiations are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company shifted to GML from cash credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites a 30% USD gold correction, rising custom duty and a stronger balance sheet, with better ratings and banking relationships. GML is a natural hedge and is cheaper than the roughly 9% cost of the current borrowings.

qa_highlights.question: Is the franchise route planned and what is the long-term business split?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchising is premature. Current brand investment is meant to make the brand franchisable later. B2B will remain, and B2C profit share is expected to rise over three to four years.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from pre-opening costs, lease accounting and muted gold price gains; quarterly EBITDA margin trend as stores open.
Store ramp-up in Surat and Rajkot against the one-year capex break-even target.
Gold price volatility on about INR400 crore inventory; hedging transition depends on bank GML sub-limits still under negotiation.
Rising debt as borrowings grow; target D/E of 1.5-2:1 depends on GML availability and rating upgrade.
Job work share (54%) and working capital cycle; customers must provide gold advances.
Shift toward 18-karat jewellery; management says its contribution is still small.
summary.management_tone: Confident on retail expansion and demand visibility, but evasive on store-level revenue forecasts, segment EBITDA (withheld for competitive reasons), and the franchise timeline. Management openly acknowledged the margin dip and pre-opening costs.
key_quotes: So we are going to transform into a retail side.
We are utilizing factory at around 50% of capacity.
Right now we are not sharing it because of competitive reasons.

adds.what: Surat large-format store (~10,000 sq ft), capex ~INR10 crores

growth.why: Management guides Q2 in line with earlier projections, backed by a full July-August order book and IIJS orders, plus store rollout (Surat, Rajkot near-term; Maninagar/Gandhinagar in Q3) with Surat capex ~INR10 crores, but no quantified FY27 revenue growth target was given.
